title: Longest Palindromic Substring
statement: You get a string. Find its longest substring (a block of consecutive letters) that reads the same forwards and backwards. If several blocks tie for longest, any one of them is accepted.

example.caption: In babad, bab and aba both work. Either one is a correct answer.

idea.sentence: Every palindrome mirrors around a centre, so try each letter and each gap between letters as a centre and grow outward while the two ends match.

jargon.plain: Text that reads the same left to right and right to left.
A run of consecutive letters. Unlike a subsequence, you cannot skip letters.
The middle of a palindrome. A letter if its length is odd, the gap between two letters if it is even.

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: n² substrings, each checked in up to n steps.

rows.name: Expand around centres
rows.note: 2n - 1 centres, each can grow up to n / 2 steps. No table needed.

rows.name: DP table (n × n)
rows.note: isPal[i][j] is true when s[i] = s[j] and the inside is a palindrome. Same time, more memory.

rows.name: Manacher
rows.note: Reuses mirror information between centres. Worth knowing, rarely asked.

fast.takeaway: A palindrome's inside is a smaller palindrome. Growing from the middle uses that without any table.

stages.title: Nothing yet
stages.note: Remember the start and length of the best palindrome. Both begin at zero.

stages.title: Grow outward
stages.note: From a centre, while the letters at l and r match, the window is a palindrome. Step both outward.

stages.title: Compare with the best
stages.note: The growth stopped. Its window is the longest palindrome at this centre. Keep it if it is longer than the best.

stages.title: Answer
stages.note: After all centres, cut out the best window.

edges.title: Even-length palindrome
edges.why: Its centre sits between two letters. Trying only letter centres would find just single letters.

edges.title: Single letter
edges.why: A lone letter is a palindrome of length 1. The odd centre finds it with no growth.

edges.title: No repeated letters
edges.why: Every answer has length 1 and all four tie. This is why tests check the length and the palindrome, not one exact string.

edges.title: Whole string
edges.why: The centre at index 3 grows until both pointers fall off the string. The bounds check stops it.

gotchas.text: Test both centre kinds. Odd centres start with l = r = c. Even centres start with l = c and r = c + 1.
After the loop, l and r are one step too far. The palindrome is s[l + 1 .. r - 1], and its length is r - l - 1.
Check the bounds before reading s[l] and s[r]. s[-1] is undefined, not an error, so a missing check can quietly give wrong answers.
s[i] is a byte, not a character. This is fine for ASCII, but for text with accents or emoji, convert to []rune first.
Slicing a string with s[a:b] copies nothing. It is cheap, but you must not go past len(s).

recap.key: Every palindrome has a centre. From each of the 2n - 1 centres, grow outward while the ends match and remember the longest.
moves: For each index c, try an odd centre (c, c) and an even centre (c, c + 1)
Grow while l >= 0, r < n and s[l] == s[r]
The window s[l + 1 .. r - 1] is this centre's best; keep it if longer
